title: Topic Classification: Authoring Disambiguated Natural Language Descriptions

steps.prompt: An agent has two topics: "Order Cancellation" and "Subscription Billing". A customer asks: "Stop my recurring monthly shipments." The agent routes to Order Cancellation and fails. How should the topic descriptions be refined?

options.label: Define explicit scope boundaries and negative triggers distinguishing recurring plans from one-off purchases
options.rationale: Explicitly defining scope boundaries and negative triggers (e.g., "do NOT use for recurring subscriptions") prevents classification ambiguity.

options.label: Consolidate both topics into a single composite topic and let the LLM evaluate all actions in a single plan
options.distractorAntipattern: Bloating topics with dozens of actions degrades tool-selection precision and increases reasoning latency.
options.rationale: Combining distinct operational domains into one massive topic dilutes semantic routing, increases tool selection confusion, and bloats context tokens.

options.label: Add keyword-matching routing rules in an orchestration Flow before passing the conversation context to Atlas
options.distractorAntipattern: Keyword rules break generative natural language understanding and fail on linguistic variations or synonyms.
options.rationale: Hardcoded keyword rules undermine the generative classification capabilities of the Atlas reasoning engine and fail when customers phrase requests conversationally.
